blocks.zh: 刷题时常见的“找规律”：2，4，8，下一个是什么？“每次乘 2”给出 16；“每次加的数递增（+2，+4，+6）”给出 14。前三个数两条规则都完全符合，可它们对下一个数的预测不一样。祖母绿的观察对 green 和 grue 也是这样：过去的数据都符合，预测却打架。
blocks.limit: 找规律题里我们默认“更简单”的规则是答案。按古德曼的思路可以追问（本站的引申，节选没有讨论“简单”）：凭什么说 green 比 grue 更简单、更自然？后面讲 bleen 和对称性的那一节有相关的论证。另外，祖母绿的例子比的不是数字规律，而是两个谓词。

label.zh: 论证的标准形式（P＝前提，C＝结论）：grue 论证（第 1–2 页）
label.en: Standard form: the grue argument (pp. 1-2)

items.en: P1: Suppose every emerald examined before time t has been green. By the definition of confirmation, each report such as 'emerald a is green' confirms 'All emeralds are green'.
items.zh: P1：设 t 之前检查过的祖母绿都是绿的。按确证定义，每条“祖母绿 a 是绿的”这样的报告都确证“所有祖母绿都是绿的”。

items.en: P2: Define 'grue': an object is grue if it is examined before t and is green, or if it is not examined before t and is blue.
items.zh: P2：定义 grue：在 t 之前被检查过并且是绿的，或者没在 t 之前被检查过并且是蓝的。

items.en: P3: Then every emerald examined so far is also grue, and by the same definition the parallel reports ('emerald a is grue', and so on) confirm 'All emeralds are grue'.
items.zh: P3：那么目前检查过的每颗祖母绿也都是 grue 的；按同一个定义，对应的报告（“祖母绿 a 是 grue 的”等等）确证“所有祖母绿都是 grue 的”。

items.en: P4: The two hypotheses make incompatible predictions about emeralds examined after t: one predicts green, the other blue, since a grue emerald examined later is blue and so not green.
items.zh: P4：两个假说对 t 之后检查的祖母绿做出不相容的预测：一个说绿，一个说蓝，因为 t 之后检查的 grue 祖母绿是蓝的，所以不是绿的。

items.en: P5: Yet we know that only the green prediction is genuinely confirmed.
items.zh: P5：可我们知道，真正被确证的只有“绿”的预测。

items.en: C: So a definition of confirmation that looks only at form gives equal support to incompatible predictions; without a criterion of lawlikeness it cannot work.
items.zh: C：所以只看形式的确证定义，会同等地支持互相冲突的预测；没有判断似律的标准，它就不能用。

title.zh: 一步步走 grue 论证（第 1–2 页）
title.en: The grue argument step by step (pp. 1-2)

steps.zh: 第 1 步：到时刻 t 为止，我们检查过的祖母绿 a、b、c……全是绿的。
steps.en: Every emerald examined up to time t (a, b, c, ...) is green.

steps.zh: 第 2 步：它们都是在 t 之前被检查的，又都是绿的，所以按定义它们也都是 grue 的。每一条“a 是绿的”都对应一条同样真的“a 是 grue 的”。
steps.en: Each was examined before t and is green, so each is also grue; every green report has a parallel, equally true grue report.

steps.zh: 第 3 步：按确证定义，绿的报告确证“所有祖母绿都是绿的”，grue 的报告同样确证“所有祖母绿都是 grue 的”。
steps.en: By the definition, the green reports confirm 'All emeralds are green', and the grue reports equally confirm 'All emeralds are grue'.

steps.zh: 第 4 步：看对 t 之后才检查的祖母绿的预测。第一个假说说：会是绿的。第二个假说说：会是 grue 的，而 t 之后才检查的东西要算 grue，就必须是蓝的。两个预测不可能都对。
steps.en: For emeralds examined after t, the first hypothesis predicts green; the second predicts grue, which for them means blue. Both cannot be right.

steps.zh: 第 5 步：我们心里很清楚，真正被确证的是“绿”的预测；可按这个定义，两者被同样好地确证了。
steps.en: We know that the green prediction is the one genuinely confirmed, yet by the definition both are equally well confirmed.

answer.zh: 同样的观察，同等地“确证”了两个互相冲突的预测。所以光看形式的确证定义出了大问题。
answer.en: The same observations equally 'confirm' two conflicting predictions, so a purely formal definition of confirmation is in serious trouble.

blocks.zh: 古德曼接着把问题推到底：只要挑一个合适的谓词，同样这些观察就能同等地确证关于其他祖母绿、甚至关于任何东西的任何预测（第 2 页）。真正被确证的只是似律假说下的预测，可我们还没有判断似律的标准（**criterion**）。没有它，这个定义就不只是放进了几个古怪的例子，而是几乎什么都排除不了，结果就是“anything confirms anything”（第 2 页）。他说，这不是以后再慢慢处理的小细节：定义要能用，必须先解决它。
blocks.en: With a suitable predicate, the same observations would equally confirm any prediction whatever, so without a criterion of lawlikeness the definition excludes almost nothing: "anything confirms anything" (p. 2).

title.zh: 自己造一个词试试（演示用，读物里没有这个词）
title.en: Try it yourself (an illustration; the word is not in the reading)

steps.zh: 仿照 grue 造一个谓词 gred：一个东西是 gred 的，当且仅当它在 t 之前被检查过并且是绿的，或者没有在 t 之前被检查过并且是红的。
steps.en: Define 'gred': examined before t and green, or not examined before t and red.

steps.zh: t 之前检查过的祖母绿全是绿的，所以它们也全是 gred 的。
steps.en: Every emerald examined before t is green, so every one is also gred.

steps.zh: 按同一个定义，这些观察也确证“所有祖母绿都是 gred 的”，也就是预测 t 之后检查的祖母绿是红的。
steps.en: By the same definition, the observations confirm 'All emeralds are gred', which predicts red emeralds after t.

steps.zh: 换成任何颜色、任何性质都行。这就是古德曼说的：只要挑合适的谓词，同样的证据可以“确证”任何预测。
steps.en: Any colour or property would do: with a suitable predicate, the same evidence 'confirms' any prediction.

answer.zh: 所以问题不在 grue 这一个怪词，而在于这个确证定义几乎什么都挡不住。
answer.en: The problem is not one odd word; the definition excludes almost nothing.

prompt.en: Objection: 'Our evidence favours green, because we have actually seen green emeralds; nobody has ever seen a grue one.' Is this right?
prompt.zh: 反驳：“证据当然支持绿，因为我们真看到的是绿的祖母绿；谁也没见过 grue 的祖母绿。”对吗？

answer.en: No. Every emerald we have seen was examined before t and was green, so by definition every one of them was also grue (p. 1). The same observations can be reported as 'this emerald is green' or as 'this emerald is grue', and both reports are true. So the evidence by itself cannot favour one hypothesis, which is why Goodman says we need a criterion of lawlikeness.
answer.zh: 不对。我们看到的每颗祖母绿都是在 t 之前被检查的、又是绿的，所以按定义每一颗也都是 grue 的（第 1 页）。同样的观察，既可以报告成“这颗是绿的”，也可以报告成“这颗是 grue 的”，两种报告都真。所以光看证据分不出哪个假说更好，这正是古德曼说需要一个似律标准的原因。

items.zh: grue 不是“到了时刻 t 会变色”。没有任何东西变色；算不算 grue，看的是颜色加上它是不是在 t 之前被检查。
items.en: Nothing changes colour at t; grue depends on colour plus time of examination.

items.zh: grue 的定义适用于一切东西，不只是祖母绿（第 1 页）。从来没被检查过的东西，也算“没有在 t 之前被检查”。
items.en: Grue is defined for all things, and never-examined things count as not examined before t.

items.zh: 古德曼同意真正被确证的是“绿”的预测；他说的是那个定义分不出来，不是说我们应该预测蓝。
items.en: Goodman agrees that green is genuinely confirmed; the definition cannot tell the difference.

items.zh: “anything confirms anything”不是说任意两句话都互相确证，而是说：挑合适的谓词，同样的证据可以同等地确证任何预测。
items.en: 'Anything confirms anything' means that with a suitable predicate the same evidence confirms any prediction.

question.en: Let t be a fixed time. Which of the following objects is grue?
question.zh: 设 t 是一个固定的时刻。下面哪个东西是 grue 的？

options.en: A green emerald examined before t.
options.zh: 一颗在 t 之前被检查过的绿色祖母绿。

options.en: A blue sapphire examined before t.
options.zh: 一颗在 t 之前被检查过的蓝宝石。

options.en: A green emerald first examined after t.
options.zh: 一颗 t 之后才第一次被检查的绿色祖母绿。

options.en: A red ruby that has never been examined.
options.zh: 一颗从来没被检查过的红宝石。

explain.zh: 选 A：在 t 之前被检查、而且是绿的，符合定义的第一种情况。B 在 t 之前被检查却是蓝的，不是 grue。C 没有在 t 之前被检查，要算 grue 必须是蓝的，它是绿的，所以不是。D 从来没被检查过，也算“没有在 t 之前被检查”，要算 grue 也必须是蓝的，它是红的，所以不是。另外记住：grue 的定义里根本没有颜色变化。
explain.en: A fits the first clause. B was examined before t but is blue; C was not examined before t and is green, not blue; D was never examined, so it would have to be blue to be grue, but it is red. Grue involves no change of colour.

title.zh: 古德曼：两种失败的补救：偷运信息与间接支持（H 与 K）
title.en: Goodman: Two Failed Fixes: Smuggled Information and Indirect Support (H vs K)

blocks.zh: 古德曼说，这个困难常常被轻视，因为表面上似乎有很容易的解决办法（第 2 页）。他把这些办法一个个拿出来检验，每个都失败了。这一节讲前两个：一是“偷运了背景信息”的说法，二是“通过相关假说间接支持”的说法。另外两个在下一节。

items.en: lawlike / accidental
items.zh: 似律的 / 偶然的
items.hint: 能 / 不能被自己的实例确证（第 1 页）。

items.en: background information
items.zh: 背景信息
items.hint: 证据之外、我们本来就知道的情况。

items.en: smuggled / tacit use
items.zh: 偷运 / 默默使用
items.hint: 没有明说，却在判断时偷偷用上了。

items.en: paradox of the ravens
items.zh: 乌鸦悖论
items.hint: 另一个关于确证的难题；节选只提了名字。

items.en: confirm / disconfirm
items.zh: 确证 / 否证
items.hint: 证据让一个假说更可信 / 更不可信。

items.en: amenability to confirmation
items.zh: 可被确证性
items.hint: 一旦找到直接的正面实例，就能被它们确证；古德曼用它来说明什么是似律性。

items.en: uniform in conductivity
items.zh: 导电性一致
items.hint: 一类东西要么都导电，要么都不导电。

items.en: circular
items.zh: 循环的
items.hint: 用要解释的东西来解释它自己。

blocks.zh: 补充（读物外）：乌鸦悖论（**paradox of the ravens**）是哲学家亨佩尔（Carl Hempel）提出的确证难题：按某些确证规则，一只白鞋似乎也能确证“所有乌鸦都是黑的”。一种常见的解释是：我们觉得奇怪，是因为偷偷用了背景知识；把这些知识明说出来，问题就消失了。节选只提到它的名字和这一点，本站不展开。
blocks.en: Outside the reading: the paradox of the ravens is Hempel's puzzle in which a white shoe seems to confirm 'All ravens are black'. The excerpt only mentions it.

label.zh: 补救一（P＝前提，C＝结论）：“偷运了背景信息”及古德曼的回应（第 2 页）
label.en: Fix 1: 'smuggled information' and Goodman's reply (p. 2)

items.en: Proposal: as in the paradox of the ravens, we tacitly use information outside the stated evidence: that pieces of the same material tend to agree in conductivity, and that the men in one audience tend to differ in their number of older brothers.
items.zh: 提议：就像乌鸦悖论那样，我们偷偷用了证据之外的信息：同一种材料的样本通常导电性相同；同一场讲座的听众，哥哥的数量通常各不相同。

items.en: P1: In the ravens case, once the smuggled information is stated openly, the definition of confirmation registers its effect properly.
items.zh: P1：在乌鸦悖论里，把偷运的信息明说出来，确证定义就能正确地反映它的作用。

items.en: P2: Here, adding statements about the conductivity of other materials, or about the older brothers of other audiences, makes no difference at all to what the definition says about the copper hypothesis or the audience hypothesis.
items.zh: P2：可在这里，加上关于其他材料导电性、关于其他听众有几个哥哥的陈述，定义对铜的假说、对听众的假说的判断一点都不变。

items.en: C: So the definition is blind to such evidence even when it is fully declared; the problem cannot be explained away as smuggled information.
items.zh: C：所以就算把证据全都摆明，这个定义也看不到它们的作用；不能用“偷运信息”把问题解释掉。

blocks.zh: 关键在于：古德曼承认信息确实被偷运了，他没有否认这一点（第 2 页）。问题是，按古德曼的说法，这个定义对这类相关证据的作用不敏感，就算把证据全都摆明也一样。为什么会这样？本站的理解：别的材料怎样、别的听众怎样，都不是这个假说自己的实例（比如“这块铜导电”），而这个定义只看实例，所以对它们视而不见。所以“把背景信息明说出来”这一招，在乌鸦悖论里管用，在这里不管用。
第二个办法古德曼认为更有希望（第 2 页）：别的证据不直接作用于这个假说，而是借道其他假说。关于其他材料的信息，确证了“所有铁都导电”“没有橡胶导电”这类假说；据说这些假说把似律性（**lawlikeness**：一旦找到正面实例就能被确证的性质）传给了“所有铜都导电”。关于其他听众的信息，则否证了“某场听众全是第三子”这类假说，从而去掉了“这场听众全是第三子”的似律性。

title.zh: 铁、锆和我桌上的东西：H 与 K（第 2–3 页）
title.en: Iron, zirconium and the things on my desk: H and K (pp. 2-3)

steps.zh: 要走这条路，就得精确说出：假说之间要怎样“相似”，才能传递似律性。
steps.en: On this route we must say precisely how hypotheses must be alike to pass on lawlikeness.

steps.zh: 支持“所有铁都导电”的证据，会提高“所有锆（**zirconium**）都导电”的似律性，却不会提高“我桌上所有东西都导电”的似律性。为什么？
steps.en: Evidence for 'All iron conducts electricity' raises the lawlikeness of 'All zirconium conducts electricity' but not of 'All the objects on my desk conduct electricity'. Why?

steps.zh: 铁和锆这两个假说，都属于一个更大的假说 H：同一种材料构成的每一类东西，导电性都一致。
steps.en: The iron and zirconium hypotheses both fall under H: every group of same-material things is uniform in conductivity.

steps.zh: 铁和桌上东西这两个假说，只属于像 K 这样的假说：每一类“要么全由同一种材料构成、要么全在一张桌子上”的东西，导电性都一致。
steps.en: The iron and desk hypotheses fall only under something like K: every group of things that either share one material or sit on one desk is uniform in conductivity.

steps.zh: 区别在于：H 涵盖的某一类有某种性质的证据，会提高 H 涵盖的另一类也有这种性质的可信度；K 却不是这样。
steps.en: The difference: evidence that one class covered by H has the property makes it more credible that another such class has it; nothing like this holds for K.

steps.zh: 可这只是在说“H 是似律的，K 不是”。我们又回到了要解决的那个问题：怎样区分似律假说和偶然假说。
steps.en: But this only amounts to calling H lawlike and K not, and we are back to the very problem we set out to solve.

answer.zh: 这个办法要用“似律”去解释“似律”，是循环的。
answer.en: The proposal uses lawlikeness to explain lawlikeness, so it is circular.

label.zh: 补救二：间接支持及古德曼的回应（第 2–3 页）
label.en: Fix 2: indirect support and Goodman's reply (pp. 2-3)

items.en: Proposal: evidence about other materials confirms related hypotheses (all iron conducts electricity; no rubber does), and these make 'All copper conducts electricity' lawlike, where lawlikeness means being confirmable by positive instances once they are found (amenability to confirmation).
items.zh: 提议：关于其他材料的证据确证了相关的假说（铁都导电、橡胶都不导电），这些假说再把似律性，也就是能被正面实例确证的性质，传给“所有铜都导电”。

items.en: P1: Then we must say precisely how hypotheses must be related for lawlikeness to pass between them.
items.zh: P1：那就必须精确说明，假说之间要有什么关系，似律性才能传过去。

items.en: P2: Evidence for the iron hypothesis supports the zirconium hypothesis but not the hypothesis about the objects on my desk.
items.zh: P2：支持铁的假说的证据，支持锆的假说，却不支持关于我桌上东西的假说。

items.en: P3: The important difference is that evidence about one class covered by H raises the credibility of claims about other such classes, while this does not hold for K.
items.zh: P3：关键的区别是：H 涵盖的某一类的证据，能提高关于 H 涵盖的其他类的说法的可信度，K 却不能。

items.en: P4: But this amounts to no more than calling H lawlike and K not lawlike.
items.zh: P4：可这只是在说 H 是似律的、K 不是。

items.en: C: So the proposal assumes the lawlike/accidental distinction that it was supposed to explain: it is circular.
items.zh: C：所以这个提议预设了它本来要解释的“似律／偶然”区分，是循环的。

blocks.zh: 同学问：“什么样的人算学霸？”你说：“成绩好的人。”“那他们为什么成绩好？”“因为他们是学霸。”绕了一圈，什么也没解释。古德曼说，H/K 这个办法也是这样：要说清哪些假说“相关”，最后只能说“H 是似律的”，又用上了要解释的东西。
blocks.limit: 学霸的循环一眼就能看出来；古德曼指出的循环藏得更深：提议表面上谈的是“假说之间的关系”，只有追问“到底是哪种关系”时才露出来。

prompt.en: Goodman treats the indirect-support proposal as more promising than the smuggled-information proposal. Why is it more promising, and why does it still fail?
prompt.zh: 古德曼认为“间接支持”比“偷运信息”更有希望。为什么更有希望？为什么还是失败？

answer.en: One reason it seems more promising (an interpretation, since Goodman simply calls it more promising) is that it explains why the extra evidence matters: it works through related hypotheses that the definition does confirm (p. 2). But it needs a precise account of which hypotheses are relevantly alike. Evidence about iron supports zirconium but not the objects on my desk, and the important difference Goodman finds between H and K comes down to calling H lawlike and K not (p. 3). So the proposal presupposes the very distinction it was meant to explain.
answer.zh: 它看起来更有希望，一个原因是（本站的理解，古德曼只说它更有希望，没说理由）：它说明了额外的证据为什么重要，因为证据通过定义确实能确证的相关假说起作用（第 2 页）。可它需要精确说明哪些假说是“相关地相似”的。铁的证据支持锆，却不支持桌上的东西；古德曼找到的 H 和 K 的关键区别，说到底只是在说 H 是似律的、K 不是（第 3 页）。所以这个提议预设了它本来要解释的区分。

items.zh: 古德曼承认背景信息确实被偷运了；他反对的是“这样就解决了问题”。
items.en: Goodman grants that information is smuggled in; he denies that this solves the problem.

items.zh: 乌鸦悖论里，把信息明说出来就能解决；这里明说了也没用。别把两者说成一样。
items.en: Declaring the information helps in the ravens case but not here.

items.zh: H 和 K 都是一般的假说；差别不在句子形式上，而在于一类的证据能不能支持其他类。
items.en: H and K differ not in form but in whether evidence about one class supports claims about others.

items.zh: 间接支持的提议失败，是因为循环，不是因为“铁和锆不相似”。
items.en: The indirect-support proposal fails because it is circular.

question.en: Why does Goodman reject the proposal that lawlikeness is passed on indirectly by related hypotheses (H versus K)?
question.zh: 古德曼为什么否定“似律性通过相关假说间接传递”这个提议（H 与 K）？

options.en: Because iron and zirconium do not really conduct electricity.
options.zh: 因为铁和锆其实不导电。

options.en: Because the relevant difference between H and K comes down to calling H lawlike and K not, so the proposal is circular.
options.zh: 因为 H 和 K 之间的关键区别，说到底只是在说 H 是似律的、K 不是，所以这个提议是循环的。

options.en: Because the proposal relies on the paradox of the ravens.
options.zh: 因为这个提议依赖乌鸦悖论。

options.en: Because the objects on a desk are always made of the same material.
options.zh: 因为桌上的东西总是由同一种材料做的。

explain.zh: 选 B（第 3 页）：要说明哪些假说“相关”，最后只能说 H 是似律的、K 不是，于是又回到了要解决的问题。A 不是古德曼的理由，他没有怀疑铁和锆导电。C 混淆了两个补救：乌鸦悖论属于第一个补救。D 与读物和常识都不符。
explain.en: B (p. 3). A is not Goodman's reason; C confuses the two fixes; D is false and not in the reading.

title.zh: 古德曼：完全普遍性与纯质谓词为何失败：bleen 与对称性
title.en: Goodman: Why Generality and Qualitative Predicates Fail: Bleen and Symmetry

blocks.zh: 古德曼说，第三个办法是最流行的（第 3 页）：偶然假说好像通常带着空间或时间上的限制，或者提到某个特定的个体，比如“这个房间里的人”“某人桌上的东西”；似律假说谈的则是“所有乌鸦”“所有铜”。于是很多人认为：完全普遍性（**complete generality**）就足以保证一个假说是似律的。古德曼说，问题是“完全普遍”很难定义。

items.en: lawlike / accidental
items.zh: 似律的 / 偶然的
items.hint: 能 / 不能被自己的实例确证。

items.en: predicate
items.zh: 谓词
items.hint: 句子里说对象“是怎样”的部分，比如“是绿的”。

items.en: complete generality
items.zh: 完全普遍性
items.hint: 不受任何空间、时间限制，也不提到任何特定个体。

items.en: sufficient condition
items.zh: 充分条件
items.hint: 只要满足它，结论就一定成立。

items.en: terms for specific individuals
items.zh: 指称特定个体的词
items.hint: 点名、描述或指向某个特定东西或地点的词，比如“这个房间”“伦敦”。

items.en: equivalent
items.zh: 等价的
items.hint: 说法不同，意思完全一样，必然同真同假。

items.en: syntactically universal hypothesis
items.zh: 句法上全称的假说
items.hint: 形如“所有 F 都是 G”的假说。

items.en: purely qualitative / nonpositional predicate
items.zh: 纯质的 / 非位置性的谓词
items.hint: 意思里不涉及任何特定时间、地点或个体的谓词。

items.en: positional predicate
items.zh: 位置性谓词
items.hint: 意思里涉及特定时间、地点或个体的谓词。

items.en: well-behaved / ill-behaved
items.zh: 表现良好 / 表现不良
items.hint: 用这个谓词写成的简单全称假说是 / 不是似律的。

items.en: bleen
items.zh: bleen（常见中译“蓝绿”）
items.hint: 和 grue（t 之前被检查且是绿的，或没在 t 之前被检查且是蓝的）配对的另一个自造谓词，定义见下。

items.en: begging the question
items.zh: 窃取论题
items.hint: 把要说明的东西偷偷当作前提来用。

items.en: dichotomy
items.zh: 二分
items.hint: 把东西分成截然不同的两类。

label.zh: 补救三（P＝前提，C＝结论；本站重构，第一角的读法见下面的提醒）：完全普遍性及古德曼的回应（第 3 页）
label.en: Fix 3: complete generality and Goodman's reply (p. 3; our reconstruction, see the note below on the first horn)

items.en: Proposal: accidental hypotheses mention particular places, times or individuals (this room, my desk), while lawlike ones are completely general (all ravens, all copper), so complete generality is enough for lawlikeness.
items.zh: 提议：偶然假说提到特定的地点、时间或个体（这个房间、我的桌子），似律假说是完全普遍的（所有乌鸦、所有铜），所以完全普遍就足以保证似律。

items.en: P1: Banning words that name, describe or point to a particular thing or place is not enough. 'All emeralds are grue' contains no such word, and any such word (as in 'men in this room') can be replaced by a predicate true of exactly the same things.
items.zh: P1：只禁止点名、描述或指向特定东西、地点的词还不够。“所有祖母绿都是 grue 的”里根本没有这种词；有这种词的地方（比如“这个房间里的人”），也总能换成一个只适用于完全相同那些东西的谓词。

items.en: P2: So we might also ban hypotheses equivalent to ones that contain such words. But banning only hypotheses that cannot be stated without such words bans nothing, since such words can always be replaced.
items.zh: P2：于是也许要连“等价于含这种词的假说”的假说一起禁止。可如果只禁止离不开这种词的假说，就什么也禁止不了，因为这种词总能换掉。

items.en: P3: And banning every hypothesis that has some equivalent containing such a word bans everything: even 'All grass is green' is equivalent to 'All grass in London or elsewhere is green'.
items.zh: P3：如果禁止一切“有某个等价说法含这种词”的假说，就什么都禁止了：连“所有草都是绿的”都等价于“伦敦或别处的所有草都是绿的”。

items.en: C: So complete generality, understood as the absence of terms for particular individuals, cannot mark off the lawlike hypotheses.
items.zh: C：所以把完全普遍性理解为“不含指称特定个体的词”，划不出似律假说。

title.zh: “等价”带来的两难（第 3 页）
title.en: The dilemma about equivalents (p. 3)

steps.zh: 先看为什么只禁个体词不够：“这个房间里的人”可以换成一个新造的谓词，比如“房间人”（演示用，指此刻在这个房间里的那几个人）。换完以后，假说里没有个体词了，可它还是那个偶然假说。
steps.en: An individual term such as 'in this room' can be replaced by a coined predicate true of exactly the same people; the hypothesis is still accidental but has no individual term.

steps.zh: 所以有人想：凡是和“含个体词的假说”等价的假说，也一律排除。可这句话有两种读法。
steps.en: So one might also exclude hypotheses equivalent to ones with individual terms. This can be read in two ways.

steps.zh: 读法一（本站按上下文逻辑的理解；第 3 页印的字句见下面的提醒）：只排除那些怎么说都离不开个体词的假说（它的所有等价说法都含个体词）。可个体词总能换成谓词，这样的假说根本不存在，于是什么也排除不了。
steps.en: Reading 1 (our reading of the logic; see the note below on the printed wording): exclude only hypotheses all of whose equivalents contain individual terms. Since such terms can always be replaced, there are none, so nothing is excluded.

steps.zh: 读法二：排除一切“有某个等价说法含个体词”的假说。可任何假说都有这样的等价说法：“所有草都是绿的”等价于“伦敦或别处的所有草都是绿的”，后者提到了伦敦。于是什么都被排除了，连最好的似律假说也不剩。
steps.en: Reading 2: exclude every hypothesis that has some equivalent with an individual term. Every hypothesis has one ('All grass is green' / 'All grass in London or elsewhere is green'), so everything is excluded.

answer.zh: 要么什么都排除不了，要么什么都排除了。完全普遍性这条路走不通。
answer.en: The proposal excludes either nothing or everything, so complete generality cannot be the criterion.

blocks.zh: 留意第 3 页右栏第一角的印刷字句。书上印的意思是：只排除“所有等价说法都不含个体词”的假说，等于什么也没排除。这句话有两种理解，结论相同。（1）照字面读也说得通：任何假说都有一个含个体词的等价说法（比如“伦敦或别处的所有草都是绿的”），所以“所有等价说法都不含个体词”的假说一个也没有，只排除它们，当然什么也没排除。（2）也可能是印刷错误，原意是“所有等价说法都含个体词”：个体词总能换成谓词，这样的假说同样一个也没有，所以也什么都没排除。本站无法确定是哪一种，上面的读法一用的是（2）。考试时不必纠结这句字句，写清两角的结论和理由即可：窄的禁令什么也排除不了；宽的禁令（只要有某个含个体词的等价说法就排除）把一切都排除了。
blocks.en: The printed first horn on p. 3 speaks of excluding only hypotheses whose equivalents are all free of individual terms. Read literally, this works: every hypothesis has some equivalent with an individual term (the grass example), so there are no such hypotheses and nothing is excluded. It may also be a misprint for hypotheses all of whose equivalents contain such terms; since such terms can always be replaced, there are none of those either. Either way this horn excludes nothing, and we cannot tell which reading is meant.

blocks.zh: 第四个办法：限制谓词的种类（第 3 页）。提议说：一个句法上全称的假说，只要它的谓词是纯质的（**purely qualitative**），也就是非位置性的（**nonpositional**），它就是似律的。古德曼说，如果“纯质”又用“等价说法里含不含个体词”来定义，只会把上面的困难再搬回来。所以提议者真正的意思是：至少对简单的谓词，看一眼它的意思，就能判断它是不是纯质的。
古德曼说，先不管“一个谓词的意思”这个说法本身就很含糊，这个主张在他看来也是错的：他根本不知道怎样判断一个谓词是纯质的还是位置性的，除非完全窃取论题（**begging the question**），也就是去问这个谓词是不是表现良好（**well-behaved**）：用它写成的简单全称假说是不是似律的（第 3 页）。这样一来，“纯质”只是“表现良好”的另一个名字，什么也没解释。

label.zh: 补救四：纯质谓词、bleen 与对称性（第 3–4 页）
label.en: Fix 4: qualitative predicates, bleen and symmetry (pp. 3-4)

items.en: Definition: an emerald is bleen if and only if either it is examined before t and is blue, or it is not examined before t and is green.
items.zh: 定义：一颗祖母绿是 bleen 的，当且仅当：要么在 t 之前被检查过并且是蓝的，要么没在 t 之前被检查过并且是绿的。

items.en: Protest: 'blue' and 'green' are purely qualitative, while 'grue' and 'bleen' are not, because their meaning refers to a particular time t.
items.zh: 抗议：blue 和 green 是纯质的，grue 和 bleen 不是，因为它们的意思里提到了特定的时刻 t。

items.en: Goodman's reply: if we start from blue and green, grue and bleen are defined with blue, green and a temporal term; but if we start from grue and bleen, blue and green are defined with grue, bleen and a temporal term.
items.zh: 古德曼的回应：从 blue 和 green 出发，grue 和 bleen 要用 blue、green 加一个时间词来定义；可从 grue 和 bleen 出发，blue 和 green 同样要用 grue、bleen 加一个时间词来定义。

items.en: For example, an emerald is green if and only if either it is examined before t and is grue, or it is not examined before t and is bleen.
items.zh: 例如：一颗祖母绿是 green 的，当且仅当：要么在 t 之前被检查过并且是 grue 的，要么没在 t 之前被检查过并且是 bleen 的。

items.en: C: So qualitativeness is entirely relative to the predicates we start from; it does not divide predicates into two kinds and cannot be the criterion of good behaviour.
items.zh: C：所以“纯质”完全取决于我们从哪些谓词出发，是相对的；它分不出两类谓词，不能当作“表现良好”的标准。

blocks.zh: 你的母语是中文：英文单词要靠中文来解释，你会觉得英文是“需要翻译的那一边”。可对一个英国同学来说正好反过来：中文才需要用英文解释。哪边“需要解释”，取决于你从哪种语言出发。古德曼说，green 和 grue 也是这样：哪个“提到了时间”，取决于你从哪组词出发。
blocks.limit: 中英文互译时不会多出一个时间词；古德曼的点更具体：两边的定义都必须用到时刻 t。另外，古德曼仍然承认 green 表现良好、grue 表现不良；他只是说“纯质”解释不了为什么。

blocks.zh: 别误会古德曼的立场：他明确说，他也认为 blue、green 是表现良好、可以放进似律假说的谓词，grue、bleen 是表现不良的（第 4 页）。他反对的是“前者纯质、后者不纯质”这个论证（他说这个论证站不住脚），以及拿“纯质”当“表现良好”标准的做法。纯质与否是相对的，它本身不能把谓词分成两类（**dichotomy**）；把“纯质”当作“表现良好”标准的人，完全忽略了这种相对性。

prompt.en: A student objects: 'We can tell that an emerald is green just by looking, without knowing the date; but to tell whether a new emerald is grue, we must know whether it was examined before t. So green really is the more basic predicate.' Does the excerpt answer this?
prompt.zh: 有同学反驳：“看一眼就知道祖母绿是不是绿的，不用知道日期；可要判断一颗新祖母绿是不是 grue，就得知道它是不是在 t 之前被检查的。所以 green 才是更基本的谓词。”节选回答了这个反驳吗？

answer.en: Not directly. Goodman's symmetry argument is about definitions: whichever pair of predicates we start from, the other pair needs a temporal term (p. 4). The student's point is about observation, which the excerpt does not discuss. A defender of Goodman might say that a speaker who started from grue and bleen would need to know the time to apply 'green', but this goes beyond the text, so it is best treated as an open question.
answer.zh: 没有直接回答。古德曼的对称性论证讲的是定义：不管从哪一对谓词出发，另一对都要用到时间词（第 4 页）。这位同学讲的是观察，节选没有讨论。替古德曼辩护的人也许会说：一个从 grue、bleen 出发的人，要用 green 时同样得知道时间；但这已经超出了读物，考试时最好当作开放问题来写。

items.zh: 对称性论证不是说 grue 的通常定义里没有时间词，而是说：从 grue、bleen 出发时，green 的定义里也有时间词。
items.en: Symmetry does not deny that grue's usual definition mentions t; it says green's definition does too when grue and bleen are basic.

items.zh: 古德曼同意 grue、bleen 表现不良；他否认的是“纯质”能解释这一点。
items.en: Goodman agrees that grue is ill-behaved; he denies that qualitativeness explains why.

items.zh: 读物里 bleen 只对祖母绿定义（第 3 页），grue 是对一切东西定义的。
items.en: In the excerpt bleen is defined only for emeralds; grue is defined for all things.

items.zh: 完全普遍性的两难：一边是什么都排除不了，一边是什么都排除了。别把两边弄反，并留意第 3 页第一角的印刷字句（见上面的提醒）。
items.en: The generality dilemma: nothing excluded on one reading, everything on the other.

question.en: How does Goodman reply to the claim that 'green' is purely qualitative while 'grue' is not, because 'grue' refers to a time t?
question.zh: 有人说 green 是纯质的、grue 不是，因为 grue 提到了时刻 t。古德曼怎么回应？

options.en: He agrees, and concludes that only 'green' can appear in lawlike hypotheses because it is qualitative.
options.zh: 他同意，并得出结论：只有 green 能出现在似律假说里，因为它是纯质的。

options.en: He argues that if we start from 'grue' and 'bleen', then 'green' must be defined with them plus a temporal term, so qualitativeness is relative.
options.zh: 他论证：如果从 grue 和 bleen 出发，green 就要用它们加一个时间词来定义，所以纯质与否是相对的。

options.en: He argues that 'grue' does not refer to any time.
options.zh: 他论证 grue 根本没有提到任何时间。

options.en: He argues that scientists actually use 'grue' in their predictions.
options.zh: 他论证科学家在预测中真的会用 grue。

explain.zh: 选 B（第 4 页）：从 grue、bleen 出发，green 就是“t 之前被检查且 grue，或者没在 t 之前被检查且 bleen”，同样带时间词，所以纯质与否是相对的。A 错：古德曼确实认为 green 表现良好，但他否认“纯质”是理由。C 错：他承认 grue 的通常定义有时间词。D 错：他承认我们不太会用 grue 做预测（第 4 页）。
explain.en: B (p. 4). A gives the wrong reason; C is false; D contradicts p. 4.

title.zh: 古德曼：为什么要在乎 grue？归纳的新谜题
title.en: Goodman: Why Worry About Grue? The New Riddle Named

blocks.zh: 讲完四个失败的办法，古德曼面对一个很自然的反驳（第 4 页）：grue 这种怪谓词（谓词：说对象“是怎样”的词），还有偶然假说，我们做预测时不太会用，何必操心？只要定义对平常用的假说管用，不就够了吗？

items.en: anomaly
items.zh: 反常结果
items.hint: 理论给出的、明显不对的结果。

items.en: theory of induction
items.zh: 归纳理论
items.hint: 说明证据怎样支持关于未观察情况的结论的理论。

items.en: philosophy of knowledge (epistemology)
items.zh: 知识哲学（认识论）
items.hint: 研究知识和证据的哲学分支。

items.en: confirmable / nonconfirmable
items.zh: 可确证的 / 不可确证的
items.hint: 古德曼在这里把“似律”等同于“可确证”，把“偶然”等同于“不可确证”。

items.en: riddle
items.zh: 谜题
items.hint: 让人困惑、还没有答案的问题。

items.en: new riddle of induction
items.zh: 归纳的新谜题
items.hint: 区分似律假说和偶然假说的标准是什么？这个还没解决的问题。

label.zh: 论证的标准形式（P＝前提，C＝结论）：为什么要在乎 grue（第 4 页）
label.en: Standard form: why grue matters (p. 4)

items.en: Objection: we are unlikely ever to use predicates like 'grue', or accidental hypotheses, when we make predictions, so a definition that works for the hypotheses we normally use is enough.
items.zh: 反驳：我们做预测时不太会用 grue 这类谓词或偶然假说，所以定义对平常用的假说管用就够了。

items.en: P1: That is true only in the sense in which we could also do without any definition, any theory of induction and any philosophy of knowledge, since daily life and science manage without them.
items.zh: P1：这话只在一种意义上对：照这么说，我们也根本不需要定义、归纳理论和知识哲学，因为日常生活和科学研究没有它们也过得去。

items.en: P2: If we want a theory at all, we cannot defend its glaring failures by pointing out that we steer clear of them in practice.
items.zh: P2：只要我们想要一个理论，就不能用“实际中能避开”来为它的严重反常开脱。

items.en: P3: The odd cases are like textbook cases of a disease: rarely met in practice, but they show most clearly the signs of a serious illness that runs through the whole theory.
items.zh: P3：这些怪例子像教科书里的典型病例：实际中很少见，却最清楚地显示出整个理论里普遍存在的严重毛病。

items.en: C: So grue reveals a serious defect in the theory of confirmation, not a curiosity that can be ignored.
items.zh: C：所以 grue 暴露的是确证理论的严重缺陷，不是可以不管的小怪事。

blocks.zh: 写程序时，有一种 bug 只在极少见的输入下才出现，比如用户输入一个超长的名字，app 就崩溃。你不能说“用户很少这样做，所以程序没问题”：这个 bug 说明代码的逻辑本身有漏洞，平常没出事只是因为没碰上。古德曼说，grue 就是确证理论的这种 bug。
blocks.limit: 程序的 bug 通常能找到原因，打个补丁就好；古德曼说，这个“bug”到现在既没有答案，也没有找答案的线索。

blocks.zh: 古德曼用了一个医学比喻：这些怪例子是“clinically pure cases”（第 4 页），就像教科书里最典型的病例：在实际中很少碰到，却把一种普遍而严重的病的症状显示得最清楚。本站的理解：平常不出事，是因为我们心里知道哪个预测真正被确证（第 2 页）；可理论本身说不出凭什么。

label.zh: 归纳的新谜题（第 4 页）
label.en: The new riddle of induction (p. 4)

items.en: Goodman concludes that so far there is no answer, and not even a promising hint of one, to the question of what separates lawlike (confirmable) hypotheses from accidental (nonconfirmable) ones.
items.zh: 古德曼的结论：是什么把似律的（可确证的）假说和偶然的（不可确证的）假说区分开？到目前为止既没有答案，连有希望的线索都没有。

items.en: A problem that seemed at first to be a small technical flaw now blocks the way to any adequate theory of confirmation.
items.zh: 起初看起来只是一个小小的技术毛病，现在挡住了建立合格的确证理论的路。

items.en: Goodman calls this problem the new riddle of induction: the problem of saying what distinguishes lawlike, confirmable hypotheses from accidental, nonconfirmable ones.
items.zh: 古德曼把这个问题叫作归纳的新谜题（**the new riddle of induction**）：说清是什么区分了似律（可确证）假说和偶然（不可确证）假说。

blocks.zh: 补充（读物外）：在这本书后面的部分，古德曼提出了他自己的回答，用到“可投射性”（**projectibility**）和“牢固度”（**entrenchment**，大致指一个谓词过去被用来做预测的历史）这些概念。节选里没有这些词，也没有给出任何解决办法。考试时按节选写：到这里为止，问题没有答案，也没有线索。
blocks.en: Outside the reading: later in the same book Goodman proposes his own answer in terms of projectibility and entrenchment. The excerpt uses neither word and offers no solution.

prompt.en: Does Goodman's new riddle show that we should stop making predictions, or that 'All emeralds are green' is not really confirmed?
prompt.zh: 古德曼的新谜题是不是说明，我们应该停止做预测，或者“所有祖母绿都是绿的”其实没有被确证？

answer.en: No. Goodman agrees that we know which of the two predictions is genuinely confirmed, and that daily life and science get along well without a theory (pp. 2, 4). His point is theoretical: no proposed definition or criterion explains why the green hypothesis is confirmable and the grue hypothesis is not. The riddle is a problem for the theory of confirmation, not a reason to give up predicting.
answer.zh: 不是。古德曼同意我们清楚哪个预测真正被确证，也承认日常生活和科学研究没有理论也过得不错（第 2、4 页）。他的问题是理论上的：没有任何一个定义或标准能说明，为什么 green 的假说可确证、grue 的假说不可确证。新谜题是确证理论的难题，不是叫我们别再预测。

items.zh: 新谜题不是把休谟的问题换个说法：休谟问从经验推论有什么根据，古德曼问哪些假说能被实例确证。节选里根本没提到休谟。
items.en: The new riddle is not Hume's problem restated, and the excerpt never mentions Hume.

items.zh: 节选没有给出解决办法；别把课外看到的答案（比如“牢固度”）当成这篇读物的观点。
items.en: The excerpt offers no solution.

items.zh: 古德曼把“似律”和“可确证”、“偶然”和“不可确证”当同义词用（第 4 页）。
items.en: Goodman uses lawlike = confirmable and accidental = nonconfirmable (p. 4).

items.zh: 古德曼没说 grue 在实践中常惹麻烦；他说的是：罕见的怪例子暴露了理论的毛病。
items.en: Goodman's point is not that grue causes practical trouble, but that rare cases reveal a flaw in the theory.

question.en: What does Goodman call 'the new riddle of induction'?
question.zh: 古德曼说的“归纳的新谜题”是什么？

options.en: The problem of saying what distinguishes lawlike (confirmable) hypotheses from accidental (nonconfirmable) ones.
options.zh: 说清是什么区分了似律（可确证）假说和偶然（不可确证）假说的问题。

options.en: The problem of proving that the future will resemble the past.
options.zh: 怎样证明未来会像过去的问题。

options.en: The puzzle of why emeralds change colour at time t.
options.zh: 祖母绿为什么会在时刻 t 变色的谜。

options.en: The paradox of the ravens.
options.zh: 乌鸦悖论。

explain.zh: 选 A（第 4 页）。B 是休谟第 4 节的问题，这篇节选没有讨论。C 误解了 grue：没有任何东西变色。D 乌鸦悖论只是第一个补救里提到的类比。
explain.en: A (p. 4). B is Hume's problem, which the excerpt does not discuss; C misreads grue; D is only mentioned in the first fix.

title.zh: 比较：休谟的旧问题与古德曼的新谜题
title.en: Comparison: Hume's Problem and Goodman's Riddle

blocks.zh: 这一节没有单独对应的读物页，而是把两篇放在一起比较，用到休谟第 7–9、12 页和古德曼第 1–4 页。复习时值得练一道比较题，比如“比较休谟的问题和古德曼的新谜题”。先记住一句话：两个问题都关于从观察过的情况推到没观察过的情况，问的却不是同一件事。
blocks.en: This section compares the two readings, drawing on Hume pp. 7-9 and 12 and Goodman pp. 1-4.

blocks.zh: 补充（读物外）：在同一本书里、这篇节选之前，古德曼专门讨论过休谟的问题，称之为“旧的归纳问题”（**the old problem of induction**），所以才把自己的问题叫“新谜题”。但节选本身一句也没提休谟。下面“grue 怎样给休谟出难题”的分析，是本站为了帮助理解做的综合，不是古德曼文中的话；考试用的时候要说明这是你自己的比较。
blocks.en: Outside the reading: earlier in the same book Goodman discusses Hume's problem as the old problem of induction, but the excerpt never mentions Hume. The link drawn below is a teaching synthesis.

items.en: induction / problem of induction
items.zh: 归纳 / 归纳问题
items.hint: 归纳＝从观察过的情况推到没观察过的情况；“归纳问题”是课程大纲给本周起的标题，也是后人给休谟论证起的名字，休谟原文里没有这两个词（见第一节和第五节的补充说明）。

items.en: new riddle of induction
items.zh: 归纳的新谜题
items.hint: 古德曼的问题：似律（可确证）假说和偶然假说靠什么区分？

items.en: custom / constant conjunction
items.zh: 习惯 / 恒常结合
items.hint: 休谟：两类东西一直一起出现（恒常结合），重复就让心灵不经推理地由一个想到另一个（习惯）。

items.en: grue / lawlike
items.zh: grue / 似律的
items.hint: grue＝t 之前被检查且绿，或没在 t 之前被检查且蓝；似律＝能被自己的实例确证。

items.en: symmetry argument
items.zh: 对称性论证
items.hint: 古德曼：从 grue、bleen 出发，green 也要用时间词来定义，所以“纯质”是相对的。

items.en: synthesis
items.zh: 综合
items.hint: 把两篇读物自己连起来的分析；要说明这是你的比较，不是作者的原话。

label.zh: 比较题可以这样写
label.en: Sentences for a comparison answer

items.en: Hume asks what grounds any inference from past experience to the future; Goodman asks which hypotheses are confirmed by their instances.
items.zh: 休谟问：从过去经验推到将来，根据是什么？古德曼问：哪些假说能被它们的实例确证？

items.en: Hume argues that no reasoning, demonstrative or probable, supports the step from past to future, and that custom produces it instead.
items.zh: 休谟论证：证明推理和或然推理都支持不了从过去到将来这一步，推动它的是习惯。

items.en: Goodman argues that a definition of confirmation based on form alone cannot separate lawlike from accidental hypotheses, as grue shows, and that every proposed criterion fails.
items.zh: 古德曼论证：只看形式的确证定义分不出似律假说和偶然假说，grue 就是证明；别人提出的标准也都失败了。

items.en: In my comparison, both reject purely logical or formal answers, but Hume ends with an account of human nature, while Goodman's excerpt ends with an unsolved riddle.
items.zh: 按我的比较，两人都拒绝纯逻辑、纯形式的答案；但休谟最后给出了一种关于人性的说明，古德曼的节选最后留下一个没解决的谜题。

blocks.zh: 两篇怎么连起来？一种思路是（本站的综合）：休谟说，一切从经验来的推论，都假定未来会像过去、相似的可感性质会伴随相似的力量（休谟第 9 页）。可是“像过去”是在哪方面像？t 之前检查过的祖母绿，一贯是绿的，也一贯是 grue 的。所以就算接受休谟的这个原则，它也没告诉我们该预测“绿”还是“grue”（也就是 t 之后检查的是蓝的）。

title.zh: 用祖母绿试一试休谟的原则（本站的综合，不是古德曼文中的话）
title.en: Testing Hume's principle on emeralds (a synthesis, not in Goodman's text)

steps.zh: 休谟的原则：未来会像过去（休谟第 9 页）。
steps.en: Hume's principle: the future will resemble the past (Hume p. 9).

steps.zh: 过去：t 之前检查过的祖母绿全是绿的，也全是 grue 的（古德曼第 1 页）。
steps.en: The past: every emerald examined before t was green, and also grue (Goodman p. 1).

steps.zh: 预测一：未来在“绿”这一点上像过去，所以 t 之后检查的祖母绿是绿的。
steps.en: Prediction 1: the future resembles the past in being green, so later emeralds will be green.

steps.zh: 预测二：未来在“grue”这一点上像过去，所以 t 之后检查的祖母绿是 grue 的，也就是蓝的。
steps.en: Prediction 2: the future resembles the past in being grue, so later emeralds will be grue, that is, blue.

steps.zh: 两个预测都说“未来像过去”，却互相冲突。所以光有休谟的原则还不够，还要说明“在哪方面像”，这正是古德曼的新谜题。
steps.en: Both predictions say the future will resemble the past, yet they conflict. The principle alone is not enough; we need to know in which respect, which is Goodman's riddle.

answer.zh: 休谟的原则没说在哪方面相似；grue 说明，这个问题不解决，“未来像过去”本身给不出确定的预测。
answer.en: Hume's principle does not say in which respect the future resembles the past; grue shows that without an answer it yields no definite prediction.

blocks.zh: 习惯也是一样（仍是本站的综合）：休谟说，习惯来自恒常结合（休谟第 12 页）。可观察到的祖母绿，既一直和“绿”结合在一起，也一直和“grue”结合在一起。习惯为什么让我们期待绿而不是 grue？有人会说“因为绿是纯质的、grue 提到了时间”，可古德曼的对称性论证（古德曼第 4 页）正好堵住了这条路。两人还有一个共同点：都不接受纯逻辑、纯形式的解决。

prompt.en: Short essay: Does Goodman's grue example show that, even if we grant Hume's assumption that the future will resemble the past, we still lack an account of which predictions experience supports?
prompt.zh: 小论文题：古德曼的 grue 例子是否表明，就算我们承认休谟“未来会像过去”的预设，仍然说不清经验支持哪些预测？

answer.en: Yes, in an important sense. Hume shows that the step from past to future rests on no reasoning, only on the assumption that the future will resemble the past and on custom (Hume pp. 7-9, 12). Goodman shows that past emeralds are uniformly green and uniformly grue, so resemblance to the past does not settle whether to predict green or blue (Goodman pp. 1-2). Since his symmetry argument blocks the reply that green is the qualitative predicate (p. 4), we still need an account of which hypotheses experience confirms. This link is my own synthesis, because Goodman's excerpt never mentions Hume.
answer.zh: 可以答“是”。休谟说明从过去到将来这一步不靠推理，只靠“未来像过去”的预设和习惯（休谟第 7–9、12 页）。古德曼说明，过去的祖母绿一贯是绿的，也一贯是 grue 的，所以“像过去”决定不了该预测绿还是蓝（古德曼第 1–2 页）。对称性论证又堵住了“绿才是纯质的”这条退路（第 4 页），所以我们仍然需要说明经验确证的是哪些假说。最后注明：这个联系是你自己的比较，古德曼的节选没有提到休谟。

title.zh: 比较型小论文的写法
title.en: How to plan a comparison essay

items.en: Thesis: state in one sentence how the two problems differ and how they connect.
items.zh: 论点：一句话说清两个问题有什么不同、怎样相连。

items.en: Hume: give his dilemma in standard form (demonstrative versus probable) and his answer (custom).
items.zh: 休谟：用标准形式写出两难（证明的 vs 或然的）和他的回答（习惯）。

items.en: Goodman: define grue, give the grue argument, and state the new riddle.
items.zh: 古德曼：定义 grue，写出 grue 论证，说出新谜题。

items.en: Connection: Hume's resemblance principle does not say in which respect; past emeralds are both green and grue.
items.zh: 联系：休谟的相似原则没说在哪方面相似；过去的祖母绿既是绿的，又是 grue 的。

items.en: Objection and reply: for example, 'green is qualitative', answered by Goodman's symmetry argument.
items.zh: 反驳与回应：比如“green 是纯质的”，用古德曼的对称性论证回应。

items.en: Conclusion: restate the thesis and say that the link is your own synthesis.
items.zh: 结论：重申论点，并说明这个联系是你自己的综合。
别把两个问题混成一个：休谟问凭什么从经验推论，古德曼问哪些假说被实例确证。
items.en: Hume asks what grounds inference from experience; Goodman asks which hypotheses their instances confirm.

items.zh: 别写“古德曼解决了休谟的问题”或“古德曼在回应休谟”：节选里没有提到休谟，也没有给出解决办法。
items.en: Goodman's excerpt neither mentions nor solves Hume's problem.

items.zh: 别写“休谟证明了未来不会像过去”：他只说这一点不能靠推理证明。
items.en: Hume does not prove that the future will differ from the past.

items.zh: 休谟的结论有积极的一面（习惯在起作用）；古德曼的节选以“没有答案”结束。
items.en: Hume ends with custom; Goodman's excerpt ends with an open riddle.

question.en: Which statement best contrasts Hume's problem with Goodman's new riddle?
question.zh: 下面哪一句最准确地对比了休谟的问题和古德曼的新谜题？

options.en: Hume asks which hypotheses their instances confirm; Goodman asks whether any inference from the past to the future is justified.
options.zh: 休谟问哪些假说被实例确证；古德曼问从过去到将来的推论是否有根据。

options.en: Hume asks what grounds any inference from past to future; Goodman asks what distinguishes hypotheses that their instances confirm from those they do not.
options.zh: 休谟问从过去到将来的推论有什么根据；古德曼问能被实例确证的假说和不能被确证的假说有什么区别。

options.en: Both ask exactly the same question, but Goodman uses emeralds instead of bread.
options.zh: 两人问的是完全同一个问题，只是古德曼用祖母绿代替了面包。

options.en: Hume solves the problem with grue, and Goodman solves it with custom.
options.zh: 休谟用 grue 解决了问题，古德曼用习惯解决了问题。

explain.zh: 选 B。A 把两人对调了。C 错：两个问题不同，例子不同只是表面。D 完全弄反了：习惯是休谟的说法，grue 是古德曼的例子，而且古德曼的节选没有给出解决办法。
explain.en: B. A swaps the two authors; C wrongly treats them as one question; D reverses who says what, and Goodman's excerpt gives no solution.

summary.en: Hume divides all objects of reason into relations of ideas, which are certain and known by thought alone, and matters of fact, whose contrary can always be conceived without contradiction.
summary.zh: 休谟把理性的一切对象分为观念的关系（确定、单凭思考就能知道）和实际的事情（它的反面总能设想而不矛盾）。

summary.en: Since the contrary of any matter of fact can be clearly conceived, no matter of fact can be demonstrated; Hume's example is the proposition that the sun will not rise tomorrow.
summary.zh: 实际的事情的反面总能清楚设想，所以它不能被证明；休谟的例子是“明天太阳不会升起”。

summary.en: All reasoning about matters of fact beyond the senses and memory rests on cause and effect, as when we infer a friend's whereabouts from his letter, or past inhabitants from a watch on a desert island.
summary.zh: 一切超出感官和记忆的事实推理都靠因果，比如从信推出朋友在哪里、从荒岛上的表推出曾经有人。

summary.en: Hume argues that causes and effects are never known a priori but only from experience of constant conjunction: Adam could not tell from water's appearance that it could suffocate him.
summary.zh: 休谟论证因果从来不能先验地知道，只能从恒常结合的经验得知：亚当不能从水的样子看出它会让他窒息。

summary.en: Because an effect is a separate event from its cause, any a priori prediction is arbitrary: the billiard balls could just as conceivably both stop or the first could bounce back.
summary.zh: 因为结果和原因是两件不同的事，任何先验预测都是任意的：两个台球都停住、或者第一个弹回来，也一样想得通。

summary.en: Our senses show us only sensible qualities, such as the colour and weight of bread, never the secret powers behind them, and past experience covers only the cases observed, so the step from past cases to future cases needs explaining.
summary.zh: 感官只给我们可感性质（比如面包的颜色和重量），从不给隐秘力量；过去的经验也只涉及观察过的那些情况，所以从过去的情况到将来的情况这一步需要解释。

summary.en: Hume's dilemma: demonstrative reasoning cannot show that the future will resemble the past, because a change in the course of nature is conceivable, and probable reasoning cannot show it without arguing in a circle.
summary.zh: 休谟的两难：证明推理证明不了未来像过去，因为自然改变可以设想；或然推理要证明它，就会循环论证。

summary.en: Firm expectations come only after many uniform experiences, as the eggs show, but reason would draw the same conclusion from one instance as from a hundred, so the inference is not reasoning.
summary.zh: 稳固的期待要靠多次一贯的经验（鸡蛋），可理性从一个例子和从一百个例子得出的结论一样，所以这个推论不是推理。

summary.en: Infants and animals also learn from experience, like the child who avoids candles after being burnt, so any argument behind the inference would have to be obvious, and no one can produce one.
summary.zh: 婴儿和动物也会从经验学习（被烫过就躲开蜡烛的孩子），所以背后的论证必须一目了然，可谁也拿不出来。

summary.en: Hume's sceptical solution is that custom or habit, not reasoning, carries us from past to future; custom is the principle that makes experience useful to us.
summary.zh: 休谟的怀疑论式解决：带我们从过去走向将来的是习惯，不是推理；是习惯让经验对我们有用。

summary.en: For Hume, belief differs from imagination not in its content but in how it feels: it is a more vivid, firm and steady conception, produced by a present impression together with custom.
summary.zh: 在休谟看来，信念和想象的区别不在内容，而在感受：它是更生动、更牢固、更稳定的构想，由当下的印象加上习惯产生。

summary.en: Goodman argues that confirmation depends on more than syntactical form: a conducting piece of copper confirms 'All copper conducts electricity', but a third son in this room does not confirm 'All men now in this room are third sons'.
summary.zh: 古德曼论证确证不只看句法形式：导电的铜确证“所有铜都导电”，房间里的一个第三子却不确证“房间里所有男人都是第三子”。

summary.en: A lawlike hypothesis can be confirmed by its instances whether or not it is true; an accidental generality cannot.
summary.zh: 似律假说无论真假都能被实例确证；偶然概括不能。

summary.en: An object is grue if it is examined before t and green, or not examined before t and blue; the same evidence then equally confirms 'All emeralds are green' and 'All emeralds are grue', which conflict about emeralds examined later.
summary.zh: 一个东西是 grue 的：在 t 之前被检查且是绿的，或者没在 t 之前被检查且是蓝的。于是同样的证据同等地确证“所有祖母绿都是绿的”和“所有祖母绿都是 grue 的”，两者对以后检查的祖母绿预测冲突。

summary.en: Goodman rejects four fixes: declaring smuggled information changes nothing, indirect support is circular, complete generality excludes nothing or everything, and qualitativeness is relative.
summary.zh: 古德曼否定了四个补救：把偷运的信息明说出来也不改变什么；间接支持是循环的；完全普遍性要么什么也排除不了，要么全排除；纯质是相对的。

summary.en: Goodman calls the unsolved problem of what distinguishes lawlike from accidental hypotheses the new riddle of induction, which differs from Hume's question of what grounds inference from experience.
summary.zh: 古德曼把“似律假说和偶然假说靠什么区分”这个没解决的问题叫作归纳的新谜题；它和休谟“从经验推论有什么根据”的问题不同。

examFocus.en: Classify statements as relations of ideas or matters of fact, and explain the contradiction test.
examFocus.zh: 很适合出选择题：判断一句话是观念的关系还是实际的事情；标准是否定它会不会矛盾。

examFocus.en: Explain why causal knowledge is not a priori, using Adam and the billiard balls.
examFocus.zh: 适合出简答题：用亚当和台球说明因果知识不是先验的。

examFocus.en: Explain sensible qualities versus secret powers (bread) and the missing medium between 'has been' and 'will be'.
examFocus.zh: 可感性质和隐秘力量（面包）；“一直如此”和“将会如此”之间缺少的中介。

examFocus.en: Reconstruct Hume's dilemma in standard form and say which horn fails by circularity and which fails because the contrary is conceivable.
examFocus.zh: 适合出论述题：用标准形式写出两难，说清哪一角失败是因为循环、哪一角是因为反面可设想。

examFocus.en: Explain what the eggs and the child and the candle show, and Hume's agent-versus-philosopher reply.
examFocus.zh: 鸡蛋、孩子和蜡烛各说明什么；行动者和哲学家的区分。

examFocus.en: Define custom or habit and explain why Hume calls his solution sceptical.
examFocus.zh: 习惯的定义；为什么叫“怀疑论式的解决”；它是解决还是换了话题。

examFocus.en: Explain how belief differs from imagination, and name the three principles of association.
examFocus.zh: 信念和想象的区别（在感受，不在内容）；三条联想原则：相似、接近、因果。

examFocus.en: Distinguish lawlike from accidental hypotheses with copper and third sons.
examFocus.zh: 用铜和第三子区分似律和偶然；似律不等于真。

examFocus.en: Define grue, decide whether sample objects are grue, and explain why the same evidence confirms incompatible predictions.
examFocus.zh: 定义 grue，判断某个东西是不是 grue，并解释同样的证据为什么确证相互冲突的预测。

examFocus.en: Explain why the smuggled-information fix and the indirect-support fix (H and K) fail.
examFocus.zh: 偷运信息和间接支持（H 与 K）为什么失败：后者是循环。

examFocus.en: Explain Goodman's symmetry argument with bleen and why qualitativeness is relative.
examFocus.zh: 用 bleen 讲清对称性论证：纯质是相对的。

examFocus.en: State the new riddle of induction and Goodman's reply to 'why worry about grue?'.
examFocus.zh: 说出新谜题的定义，以及古德曼对“为什么要在乎 grue”的回应。

examFocus.en: Compare Hume's problem with Goodman's riddle in a short essay, saying that the link between them is your own synthesis.
examFocus.zh: 小论文：比较休谟的问题和古德曼的新谜题；说明两者的联系是你自己的综合。
